subject: Private VPC deployment follow-up: networking & allowlist next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@brightretail.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-06-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private VPC deployment follow-up: networking & allowlist next steps

Hi Daniel — great to meet yesterday, thanks for the time. Per our discovery call, it sounds like BrightRetail is leaning toward a Private deployment (VPC) for data isolation and compliance, but you wanted to confirm networking approach (AWS PrivateLink vs VPC peering) and the IP allowlist/egress requirements.

Quick recap and asks so we can get your infra team unblocked: 
- Goal: Private VPC deployment in us-west-2 with dedicated control-plane access from your VPC (no public ingress).
- Options discussed: AWS PrivateLink (recommended for minimal routing changes) OR VPC peering (if you prefer direct routing).
- Info we need from you:
  1) Preferred connectivity model (PrivateLink or peering)?
  2) If peering: target CIDR(s) for peering and expected egress IPs we should announce/allow.
  3) If PrivateLink: do you have a VPC endpoint service policy or should we provide the service name and connection instructions?
  4) Any proxy/NAT between your app and the endpoint (we need outbound IP ranges for allowlist).
  5) Preferred port ranges (HTTPS 443 is default; call out if you require additional ports).

I've attached a short networking checklist and our typical diagram to make it easier for your infra team. Next steps: if you can share the VPC diagram + contact for your network engineer, we can schedule a 30-min joint call (Sean and Vivek will join) to finalize the peering/endpoint config and timeline.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com
Redwood Inference
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@brightretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: IT Ops <it-ops@brightretail.com>, BrightRetail Security <security@brightretail.com>
Date: 2027-06-10T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment follow-up: networking & allowlist next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the summary and the doc. Quick answers from our side: 
- We prefer PrivateLink initially to avoid changing our routing tables and because it fits our security posture.
- We do have an outbound NAT/egress through a managed NAT gateway — Im including IT Ops on this thread to provide exact egress IPs.
- Ports: HTTPS 443 only, no additional ports planned.

IT Ops, can you confirm the egress IP range for connections to an external service and whether you need the service name or a list of endpoints for allowlisting? Also attaching our VPC diagram (v1) for context.

— Daniel

On behalf of BrightRetail VP of Product
From: IT Ops <it-ops@brightretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@brightretail.com>
Cc: BrightRetail Security <security@brightretail.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-06-10T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment follow-up: networking & allowlist next steps

Marissa / team — attaching the VPC diagram we referenced (attached to their reply). Egress IPs from our NAT gateway are 18.204.12.0/24 and 52.12.34.128/26 (these are the ranges we can allowlist). We prefer PrivateLink too; please provide the ServiceName and we'll request service acceptance on our side.

Notes:
- We are AWS-only in us-west-2.
- We want TLS mutual auth if possible (we'll confirm cert process with security).
- We will only allow port 443 outbound to the endpoint.

Next action: please send the PrivateLink service name + any required VPC endpoint policy JSON, and we'll try to get the request accepted by EOD Wednesday.

Thanks,
BrightRetail IT Ops
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@brightretail.com>, IT Ops <it-ops@brightretail.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-06-11T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment follow-up: networking & allowlist next steps

Thanks — this is perfect. Sean and Vivek, tagging you to deliver the PrivateLink details and the minimal endpoint policy.

Sean: can you provide the following by EOD today so BrightRetail can raise the endpoint connection?
- AWS PrivateLink ServiceName (com.amazonaws.vpce-svc-xxxxxxxx)
- Minimal VPC Endpoint Policy (we typically provide a single-line JSON that limits connections to the BrightRetail account)
- TLS mTLS options and cert exchange flow (if Vivek can confirm whether we support client certs for the control plane)
- Any outbound IPs BrightRetail should allow in addition to the NAT ranges they provided (currently only 443 planned).

If it's easier, let's set a 30-min call at 1:30pm PT today — I can invite BrightRetail and we can walk through acceptance + testing.

Attachment: redwood_private_vpc_networking_checklist.pdf (networking checklist)

Thanks — Marissa
